page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.6xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, delivering 24 dedicated vCPUs across 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The configuration includes 24.0 GB of system memory, providing a lean ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware accelerators are absent with zero GPUs, and no local disk storage is bundled, requiring the use of network-attached block storage. Baseline networking throughput is provisioned at 8 Gbps.

Benchmark results show balanced multi-threaded throughput accompanied by lower single-threaded metrics. The instance achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 7777.0 and a multi-core stress-ng result of 17725.14, whereas single-core scores remained lower at 1009.0 and 1107.99 respectively. Memory benchmarks demonstrate 96.51 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 37.21 GB/sec write bandwidth, supporting multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 84.72 GB/sec. Redis SET benchmark throughput registered 17.02 million operations per second, alongside 13.45 GB/sec throughput in static web serving tests.

With its 1:1 GB-per-vCPU allocation, the ecs.ic5.6xlarge offers cost-effective CPU resource density for workloads that parallelize cleanly without demanding large memory capacity. The lack of onboard storage and modest single-core performance make it less optimal for disk-intensive or single-thread bound workloads. It serves effectively as a host for Clang software compilation pipelines, batch processing queues, static web delivery, and distributed worker nodes.
